The quantitative pipeline integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) for multi-horizon sequence forecasting, CatBoost to manage complex categorical splits, Random Forest (RF) for baseline variance stability, and XGBoost (XGB) for robust residual loss optimization. Macroeconomic volatility regimes are classified via BIRCH unsupervised clustering applied to high-frequency order book microstructure, while text-based market sentiment is derived from VADER news velocity enriched by Gemini Flash semantic reasoning.

#### 4. REAL-TIME CONTEXTUAL ENRICHMENT

The post-close settlement for Monday, September 14, 2026, reflects steady institutional reallocation as market participants position ahead of upcoming macroeconomic data releases and central bank guidance. Market-on-close (MOC) imbalances leaned moderately to the buy side, led by sustained accumulation in mega-cap technology stalwarts like NVIDIA (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT). These sentiment leaders continue to benefit from robust secular tailwinds, underpinned by resilient enterprise software spending and multi-year data center backlogs. 

Conversely, friction names such as Tesla (TSLA) and Boeing (BA) face persistent headwinds. TSLA contends with ongoing margin pressure stemming from aggressive global pricing strategies, while BA continues to navigate stringent regulatory oversight and production rate bottlenecks that delay its cash flow recovery timeline. Analyst revisions over the past week have skewed positively for semiconductor and cloud infrastructure providers, while cyclical industrials and discretionary names face selective downward revisions. Monetary policy expectations remain anchored on a soft-landing scenario, supporting risk assets despite elevated valuations.
